blocked_not_decoupled.reason: Exercises POST /bff/v1/commands via services.control_plane.bff.command_adapters.router.create_command_adapters_router(service=CommandAdapterService(..., validators=_VALIDATORS)). CommandAdapterService's generic pipeline (idempotency, confirm-token, two-man-sign, foundation/audit envelopes, require_final_command_preconditions) is already extracted into command_adapters/service.py and command_adapters/preconditions.py and is reusable, but the ~35 per-command-type _validate_* functions this task's assertions depend on (main.py ~2644-3850+, referenced via the _VALIDATORS dict at main.py ~4559) are still defined only inline in main.py, closing over main.py's own module globals (read_store, _capabilities_for_identity, redact_evidence_refs). validators= is optional on CommandAdapterService (defaults to {}); mounting the router without it would silently drop the required-field/role/business-state checks this file's tests assert on, which is not a faithful decoupling. Confirmed via git show 59acb0e6b (OPGAP-BE-COMMAND-ADAPTERS-V2-20260830) that this repo's own precedent test for create_command_adapters_router in isolation (tests/test_command_adapters_router.py) deliberately omits validators and does not exercise business-rule assertions. Copying the validator functions into the test file would fork production business logic as a second implementation, which acceptance criterion 2 explicitly forbids ("do not add a second router, scheduler, queue, or compatibility mechanism"). Tests currently pass unmodified via main.py; no regression, just not decoupled.
